Name: Breanna Smith
Badge: Teacher as Researcher: Cultivating Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

Looking back on this, one thing I learned about my teaching is that I need to make sure that students are actually understanding the meaning of a text. I think teachers and students alike get into this bad habit of just accepting the correct answer and moving on. It needs to be more than that. Students need to be asked more questions and annotate deeper to actually understand the meaning. I don't think I would have noticed that otherwise if it wasn't for these course modules. This helped to shift my thinking of my classroom practice to be more intentional, instead of accepting the correct answers and moving on.

What new questions or next steps are you leaving this module with? How might you continue to explore or build on this inquiry in your future teaching?:

The next steps that I am leaving this module with are having more intentional teaching and bringing students to a deeper level of understanding the meaning of text. I will be switching to social studies next year and I plan to use the say-mean-matter model in my future teaching as it is ancient history and I know that students will struggle with the meaning of a lot of the topics.
